### problem_chain

Walked from the root using only the rules and the world.

- Root: the customer asks that Calloway's construction delay cost nothing on the lock -> lock_ext_builder_delay_waiver. Its rule's prerequisite sentence: "The builder-delay waiver is not fixed until the lock ledger carries, under its own charge number, the extension charge for the days added to reach the moved closing date." At the opening the lock ledger (lock_events) holds only two lock_fee_paid rows and one lock_notice_sent row — no extension_fee charge. False at the opening. The write that brings it about: lock_ext_extension_charge (its rule books "an extension_fee charge with its own charge number and the extension days it prices").
- lock_ext_extension_charge: "The extension fee is fixed only after the lock record carries the extension it prices, its days counted in the extension days used beyond the extension days already charged on the lock ledger." Opening: extension_days_used 0, charged days 0 — no excess. False. Resolved by lock_ext_extension_days (the extension raises extension_days_used).
- lock_ext_extension_days: "For a lock whose record carries an expired date, the extension days are worked out only once its status on record reads locked again and its relocks used count includes that relock." Opening: expired_date 2026-09-26 is set, status expired, relocks_used 0. False. Resolved by lock_ext_builder_delay_relock (the only write that returns an expired lock to locked and raises relocks used).
- lock_ext_builder_delay_relock: `prerequisite: []`; its own eligibility (status expired, window day 18 <= 30, relocks 0 < max_relocks 1) holds.
- Derived tree: relock -(state_gate)-> extension_days -(value_input)-> extension_charge -(value_input)-> waiver. n = 3 prerequisite problems, value_input edges = 2 >= max(n−1,1) = 2; acyclic; owner=user problem present (extension_days, `extend_rate_lock_f01da2c0`, owner user). Topological order: relock, extension (customer), extension charge, waiver. Isomorphic to the declared prerequisite graph component (E1, E2, E3).
- Load-bearing runs (skip one write, replay the rest):
  - skip relock: the extension tool would act on an expired lock (base: "An expired lock cannot be extended and may only be relocked"); terminal status stays expired and the new expiration would be 2026-09-25 + 30 = 2026-10-25 instead of 2026-12-12; the extension charge loses the relocked step-up (no relock_fee row and no prior increments -> step 1) and its lead credit changes; no relock_fee row. The extension_days value itself stays 30 (62 days needed, capped) — the edge's weight is the gate and the terminal fields, which change. Bears weight.
  - skip extension: increments priced 0 -> extension charge 0 (and nothing to waive). Bears weight.
  - skip extension charge: no extension_fee row -> waiver has no charge to name and no amount. Bears weight.
- Parallel edges: none (each node has one out-edge).
- Tools judge no prerequisite (function bodies: relock writes status locked without reading status; extend adds days without reading status; assess writes the row without reading counters; waive writes without reading the charge).
- No-wait: see above.

## findings

- **T0-1 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (F1 on this world).** Symptom: two defensible waiver amounts. Root cause: `_difficulty.md` § findings F1 (undeclared override in base lock_extensions). Evidence: base lock_extensions "When the extension is needed because the purchase agreement's closing date moved for a builder delay, builder_delay_waiver_pct percent of the extension charge is waived under lock_builder_delay_waiver." with builder_delay_waiver_pct = 100 (120-Day Extended Lock parameters); extended lock_ext_builder_delay_waiver "… times the builder share, times the lapse rate … plus the reminder goodwill and the fee-standing goodwill, never more than the extension charge itself."; the extension here was needed because the closing moved for a builder delay (contract completion 2026-09-11, estimated completion 2026-11-06, notice 2026-09-22). Demonstrated consequence: reading 1 (base sentence) -> waiver = 100 % of 1061.82 = **1061.82**; reading 2 (extended rule) -> **1005.07** (gold). Corroborated outside the four artifacts by purchase_builder_delay ("borne by Calloway and waived on the lock", builder_delay_lock_extension_paid true for Meadow Collection) and by the persona's own expectation ("you had hoped it would be all of it"). Affected: lock.extended.yaml base lock_extensions rule / extended lock_ext_builder_delay_waiver `overwrite` and `base_policy_refs`; scored waiver amount (evaluation step 16). Previous revisions: none audited.
- **T0-2 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (F2 on this task).** The relock, extension-days and extension-charge computations each carry their only `method` factor in a mislabelled form (relock_expiry_reminder_multiplier: x0.5 / x0.75 / x1; construction_slip_cushion: 4 / 2 / 0 days; extension_step_up: x2 / x1.5 / x1). Counting honest labels, three of this task's four computations have 0 `method` factors (bound 1). GT's factor_trace labels them "(method)" without a tier that changes the algorithm. Affected: lock.extended.yaml factors of lock_ext_builder_delay_relock, lock_ext_extension_days, lock_ext_extension_charge.
- **T0-3 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (incoherent baseline, F3 on this task).** baseline.rule of the relock ("… multiplied by the expiry reminder multiplier …"), the extension charge ("… times the step-up multiplier …") and the waiver ("… times the builder share, times the lapse rate …") give no value for the named quantity; computed from baseline.rule alone the three fees have no definite number. (Read as 1, the fall-backs are 943.85 / 943.86 / 1061.82, all ≠ gold, matching GT's baseline_result — the defect is that the computation document does not say so.)
- **T0-4 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (tier read off a stamp).** relock_ltv_score_add_on is declared `cross_difficulty: purchase` and its rule computes "the loan amount on the lock divided by the contract price on the purchase agreement"; the seeded lock row carries `rate_locks.68d9a3c7….ltv_pct = 90.0`, which equals 377541 / 419490 = 90.000 % and selects the same tier (> 85 with score 712). Reading the lock's own field and reading the rule's cross-category quotient cannot be told apart by the score (both give +0.0625 -> 1415.78). The task keeps other cross-difficulty factors (occupancy, homeowner credit, binder), so the task-level cross-difficulty bound still holds.
- **T0-5 — observation (relock near-miss weak; GT's stated near-miss is not one).** GT's design_rationale names as the relock near-misses "the reminder exists, so the 'missing' tier (x0.5) is excluded; score 712 is below 720 by the record" — those are the tier evidence, not records the rule excludes, so that proof sentence is wrong in kind. A near-miss row does exist: the closed Larkspur agreement a7b0e847 (returned by the same purchase finder; contract price 489990 would put the relock LTV at 77 % and drop the add-on), excluded by "the contract price on the purchase agreement" of the lock. It is weak (the lock row names its own purchase_id), as the frozen T0-O4 says; not raised as a red. (Extension days: the 2026-08-14 notice, excluded by "latest", would flip the notice tier. Extension charge: CHG-HP-4417 and closing_extensions_used on the purchase side, excluded from "increments written" and "extension_fee charges on the lock ledger". Waiver: CHG-HP-4417 excluded by "on the lock ledger"; the 2026-08-14 notice would flip the lapse rate to 0.5.)
- **T0-6 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (proof figure contradicts the rule).** computations[relock].factor_sensitivity gives relock_expiry_reminder_multiplier baseline_result **1887.7**, and factor_trace says "baseline (x1) gives 1,887.70", while the same trace's plumbing says "gross 1,887.71" and the rule says "rounded half up to the cent": 377541 x 0.5 % = 1887.705 -> **1887.71**. The asserted figure is false by one cent (a half-cent tie resolved downward). It does not move the gold relock fee (1887.70 x 0.75 = 1415.775 -> 1415.78; 1887.71 x 0.75 = 1415.7825 -> 1415.78) and the factor bears weight either way; it shows the executable rounding used for the sensitivity run is not half up on ties.
- Observations: T0-O1 ("take care of whatever the lock needs today" authorises without naming a step); T0-O2 (persona dates the reminder "a few days before the end of that month", the ledger shows 2026-09-19 — the rule reads the ledger); T0-O3 (no record of the estimated completion date as of the expiry date; the exception reading rests on today's record plus the 2026-09-22 notice); T0-O5 (`lock_fee_held` 943.85 equals the ledger aggregate of the held credit — it is the base charter's declared account field, so not raised as a stamp red); charter-global O1–O9 in `_difficulty.md`.
